[[Defensive end]] | birth_date = {{Birth date|1952|4|5|mf=y}} | birth_place = [[Memphis, Tennessee]], U.S. | death_date = {{Death date and age|2012|7|12|1952|4|5|mf=y}} | death_place = [[Salisbury, North Carolina]], U.S. | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 4 | weight_lb = 252 | college = [[Tennessee State Tigers football|Tennessee State]] | draftyear=1975 | draftround=4 | draftpick=85 | teams= * [[San Francisco 49ers]] ({{NFL Year|1975}}–{{NFL Year|1978}}) * [[Detroit Lions]] ({{NFL Year|1979}}) | highlights = * First-team [[All-Pro]] ([[1977 All-Pro Team|1977]]) * 2× [[Pro Bowl]] ([[1977 Pro Bowl|1976]], [[1978 Pro Bowl|1977]]) |statlabel1=[[Quarterback sack|Sacks]] |statvalue1=34.5 |statlabel2=[[Fumble|Fumble recoveries]] |statvalue2=4 |statlabel3=[[Touchdown|Defensive TDs]] |statvalue3=1 |pfr=E/ELAMCLE01 }} '''Cleveland Elam''' (April 5, 1952 – July 12, 2012) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive tackle]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[San Francisco 49ers]] and [[Detroit Lions]] in an injury-shortened five-year career that lasted from 1975 to 1979. Elam played [[college football]] at [[Tennessee State University]] and was drafted in the fourth round of the [[1975 NFL draft]] by the 49ers. He was a two time [[Pro Bowl]]er in 1976 and 1977. Elam was married to his wife Blanche and had four children. '''Clifford Henry Frazier''' (23 November 1952 – 17 August 2014) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player and actor.   Born in [[St. Louis, Missouri]], he was a [[defensive tackle]] for the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], starting 12 of 14 games for the Chiefs in 1977.<ref name=frazier>{{cite web|title=Cliff Frazier|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FrazCl20.htm|publisher=Pro Football Reference}}</ref>  He had played college football for the [[UCLA Bruins]], where he was a member of their 1976 [[Rose Bowl Game]] championship team.<ref name=frazier/><ref>{{cite web|title=Dynamite Bruins Stagger Ohio St.|newspaper=[[The Spokesman-Review]]|date=January 2, 1976|page=34|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1314&dat=19760102&id=fr4RAAAAIBAJ&sjid=dO0DAAAAIBAJ&pg=7125,444489&hl=en|accessdate=2015-09-07}}</ref><ref name=camp>{{cite news|title=Cliff Frazier Never Left Camp|newspaper=[[The Fort Scott Tribune]]|date=August 5, 1976|page=10|accessdate=2015-09-07|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1906&dat=19760805&id=y9chAAAAIBAJ&sjid=bp8FAAAAIBAJ&pg=3946,5755613&hl=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Chiefs Feel Good About Their Picks|newspaper=[[Lawrence Journal-World]]|date=April 7, 1976|page=16|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=2199&dat=19760407&id=vrgxAAAAIBAJ&sjid=euUFAAAAIBAJ&pg=5582,1422620&hl=en|accessdate=2015-09-07}}</ref>  He was selected for the [[College All-Star Game]] after his senior year.<ref>{{cite news|title=Football All-Stars Selected|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1893&dat=19760516&id=77QtAAAAIBAJ&sjid=MtUEAAAAIBAJ&pg=4227,1684835&hl=en|accessdate=2015-09-07|newspaper=[[The Southeast Missourian]]|date=May 16, 1976|page=18}}</ref>

Frazier was the 41st pick in the 2nd round of the [[1976 NFL draft]] by the Chiefs.<ref name=frazier/>  He was traded to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] before the 1976 season in exchange for two future draft picks.<ref name=camp/>  The Eagles traded him to the [[Los Angeles Rams]] after the season, but the Rams cut him.<ref name=back>{{cite news|title=Frazier Back, Waddell Cut By Chiefs|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=2199&dat=19770907&id=Tns1AAAAIBAJ&sjid=DuYFAAAAIBAJ&pg=2381,796094&hl=en|newspaper=[[Lawrence Journal-World]]|date=September 7, 1977|page=19|accessdate=2015-09-07}}</ref>  The Chiefs re-signed him before the 1977 season.<ref name=back/><ref>{{cite news|title=Transactions|newspaper=[[Times-News (Hendersonville, North Carolina)|The Times-News]]|page=13|date=September 7, 1977|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1665&dat=19770907&id=UaBPAAAAIBAJ&sjid=pyQEAAAAIBAJ&pg=1218,785619&hl=en|accessdate=2015-09-07}}</ref>  After one season with the Chiefs, Frazier decided to retire.<ref>{{cite news|title=Chiefs' Frazier Won't Be Back|newspaper=[[The Palm Beach Post]]|date=July 9, 1978|page=E14|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1964&dat=19780709&id=I_0sAAAAIBAJ&sjid=HM0FAAAAIBAJ&pg=6783,4862382&hl=en|accessdate=2015-09-07}}{{Dead link|date=October 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

After retiring from professional football, Frazier had roles in several films, including [[North Dallas Forty]], [[Vice Squad (1982 film)|Vice Squad]] and [[House Party (film)|House Party]].  He played the character of Jethro Snell in 79 (of 80) episodes of [[HBO]]'s football comedy [[1st & Ten (HBO TV series)|1st & 10]] between 1984 and 1991.
